1. The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a) Issue order or direction or writ in the nature of mandamus or any other writ to the respondents to issue DRC to the petitioner to an extent of 9666.24 sq. mts (104046.54 sq. ft) within a time to be fixed by this hon'ble Court as per Annexure-D.
b) Pass an order to pay damages at the market rate along with a quest at 1.5 times of the area of land relinquished for an area of NC: 2023:KHC:46518 9666.24 sq. mts (104046.54 sq. ft) consisting of land and building as on the date of Relinquishment Deed dated 04.01.20165 as per Annexure-D.

sentences.text: The petitioner claims that he is the owner of the guntas excluding 2 guntas of karab and Sy.No.328 measuring 1 acre 34 guntas excluding 5 guntas of karab, both the properties situated at Kalkere village, K.R.Puram hobli, Bangalore East Taluk.

3. The Government of Karnataka vide notification dated 18.01.2005 had stipulated that in the event of the land of a private citizen being utilized for the purpose of widening of road, formation of new road or any other public purpose, Transferable Development Rights Certificate (DRC) would be issued taking into consideration the land utilized as also the value of the building if any situate on the said land required to be NC: 2023:KHC:46518 demolished.

The BBMP vide notification dated 29.07.2009, took up the work of widening of the road from Banaswadi - Horamavu going through Kalkere, K Channasandra up to Rampura Cross and in that view of the matter, 1029 sq. mts of the land was required in Sy.No.327 and 328, described herein above, belonging to the petitioner.
4. In furtherance of the same, Transferable Development Rights (TDR) being required to be granted.
A Relinquishment Deed came to be executed by the petitioner on 01.04.2015 whereunder, it was agreed that certain TDR certificate will have to be issued.

The same not being acted upon, the petitioner had submitted various representations and when the said representations have not been considered, the petitioner is before this Court seeking the aforesaid relief's.

5. On the appearance of a counsel for the BBMP, BBMP was directed to clarify and make submission as to NC: 2023:KHC:46518 why there is such an extraordinary delay of nearly eight years in consideration of the applications/representations of the petitioner and why TDR certification has not been issued.

6. In pursuance of the same, the learned counsel Sri Monesh Kumar upon obtaining instructions and getting a survey done has filed a memo on 15.12.2023 stating that the relinquishment deed which had been executed is not proper inasmuch as there is a mischief played in the said document and what has been used by the corporation is only 1089.31 sq. mts., that is 512.59 sq. mts. in Sy.No.327 and 576.72 sq. mts., in Sy.No.328.

There being no building constructed thereon, the question of calculation of building value converted into land value in the Relinquishment Deed in terms of Schedule-B thereof did not arise and this item being flagged by some of the officers resulted in a preliminary enquiry being made which delayed the proceedings.
The NC: 2023:KHC:46518 respondent-Corporation is always willing to make available the TDR certificate on the land which has been acquired and not as regards the building which did not exist.

7. The learned counsel for the petitioner had earlier on 17.11.2023 made a submission that the petitioner is only claiming TDR in respect of the land and not in respect of the building and the said submission was recorded in the said order.
8.

The petitioner has filed a memo dated 18.12.2023 which reads as under:

sentences.text: Road Infrastructure K.R.Puram Division.

Veracity of the claim of existence of building investigated and resurvey of land utilized for road widening conducted, Rectification of Relinquishment Deed is done without Building extent for land area of 1089.31 Sqm and registered in the Office of Sub-register Shivajinagara (Mahadevapura) No.MDP-1-07306- 2023-24, dated: 15.12.2023.
Letter for Khatha Bifurcation issued to ARO Horamavu as per the Rectified Relinquishment Deed on 16.12.2023.
Provisional Acceptance Letter shall be issued after Khatha Bifurcation."

10. From the above, it is clear that the extent of land which is made use of by the Corporation for the purpose of widening of the road is only 1089.31 sq. mts. and there is no building which was in existence let alone demolished or otherwise.

Schedule-B to the Relinquishment Deed dated 01.04.2015 indicates that the land relinquished is 1029 sq. mts. and building value converted into land is worked out at 5415.16 sq. mts. which is not the correct position.

It is very clear from the same that this building value has been added to the Relinquishment Deed so as to make available DRC to the petitioner by the concerned officers probably on account of collusion between the concerned officers and the petitioner.
It is also clear - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:46518 from the original relief which had sought for, that the petitioner had claimed DRC for 9666.24 sq. mts. and not for 1029 sq. mts. or 1089.31 sq. mts.

This mischief which has occurred is at the cost of the State and the tax payer inasmuch as DRC would have to be issued by the BBMP to the person like the petitioner from and out of the funds of BBMP/BDA.
It is a clear case where the officers of BBMP and the petitioner have colluded with each other to cheat and deprive the Corporation and its property.

11. Respondent No.2 is therefore directed to initiate necessary departmental enquiry against all the officers concerned as regards such fraudulent acts which amounts to cheating of the Corporation and hence the public exchequer.
If petitioner is also found to be in collusion of the same, to take necessary action against the petitioner, if necessary, by filing criminal complaint/s.

In view of the situation that has arisen, I am of the opinion that general directions have to be issued to the Chief Commissioner, Corporation when certification is made of assessing the land value in respect of the acquired land as well as building thereon in all future cases.

ORDER a) The writ petition is partly allowed.

- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:46518 b) Respondent No.2 shall forward a recommendation for issuance of DRC to respondent No.3 as regard the extent of 1089.31 sq. mts., within 30 days from today, which shall be considered by respondent No.3 within a period of 15 days thereafter.
c) Respondent No.2 to institute necessary enquiry proceedings against all concerned within a period of 15 days from the date of receipt of copy of this order as per observations made herein above.

d) Respondent No.2 to also place on record the Standard Operating Procedure prepared on the basis of the above guidelines within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
e) Though the matter is disposed, re-list on 29.01.2024 at 2.30 p.m., for reporting compliance.
